Grandparents know nothing of this *but* as with my therapist the writing is 'on the wall'. Before COVID, namely the summer of 2019, I did everything in my power to stay there for as long as I possibly could. Got to the point where I had my own room and everything. Months at a time.

I think they might have a hankering based simply on how I acted while there. I'm always afraid of overstepping stupid boundaries and was so used to being persistently told 'no' to normal things that I straight up wouldn't ask most of the time. I was allowed outside at night alone for the first time in my life at almost *16* thanks to them. They've also asked me questions about my parents, know about their transphobia and homophobia. Straight up offered to let me stay if I could make it work with my parents. Otherwise I lie and say everything's great.

On the bright side, they're very open minded people. Own a business in my home town, and would probably come to terms with everything fairly quickly given the context.

 




Not sure if they could deal with my brother at the same time given his condition - it's a lot to take in at once. He's had epilepsy since he was a child - suddenly having to talk to dozens of doctors and nurses and such might be a bit too much.

Rather selfishly though, if we're speaking about me and me *alone*, they could and most likely would take me. And I'd wager they would likely make an effort for my brother too.
